The successful candidate possesses a Master's Degree from an ARC-PA accredited program or a doctoral degree (M.D.
Exceptions to the above requirements may be made for individuals with exceptional promise as educators with professional development and engagement to pursue education as a primary goal.

Prior higher education experience (in a Physician Associate/Assistant program for PA applicants) and experience in supporting diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts within an organization are highly preferred but not required.
PA applicants must also have a minimum of 3 years of clinical experience;
candidates must have a minimum of 5 years of clinical experience;
Provides high-quality student instruction and teaches in areas of clinical expertise;
Coordinates instruction (i.e., serves as Course Director) within designated courses;
Evaluates student performance (e.g., written assignments, examinations, research projects, objective structured clinical examinations [OSCEs], lab practicals);
Engages in the academic advising of students;
Provides remedial instruction as needed;

Assists the Director of Didactic Education with the design, implementation, coordination, evaluation, and long-term management of didactic courses to ensure the curriculum is fully compliant with ARC-PA Standards;
Participates in ongoing accreditation activities, as well as continuous programmatic and curricular evaluation;
Collaborates with Program Director and other principal faculty to develop, review, and revise the mission statement, goals, and competencies of the program as necessary;
Participates in the PA program’s admissions process, including student recruitment, review of applications, evaluation of candidates, and final selection for admission;
Assists clinical site development and ongoing clinical site monitoring to ensure the quality and sufficiency of SCPEs;

Engages in faculty development activities through ongoing clinical practice and/or continuous education in order to remain aware of issues impacting Physician Associate/Assistant education and clinical practice;
Fosters academic and clinical collaborations with other programs in the School of Health Sciences, School of Pharmacy, and the Henry E. Riggs School of Applied Life Sciences;
Engages in active scholarship and service;
Serves in appropriate committees in the School of Health Sciences;
Performs other duties as determined by the Director of Didactic Education, Director of Clinical Education, Program Director, and/or the Dean of the School of Health Sciences.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a member of a team and collaboratively with other departments.

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to effectively communicate, both verbally and in writing; possess the ability to listen to all points of view, build consensus, and inform others of policies and decisions.
Demonstrated ability to analyze and present complex issues to diverse individuals and groups.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks and adapt to changing priorities.
Experience working with a diverse campus community and possess a commitment to equity and inclusion.
